title: Fundamental particle masses may still have simple ratios

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Fundamental particle masses may still have simple ratios

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Although observed elementary particle masses are not in simple ratios (unlike electric charges), truly fundamental particle masses may still have simple relations, because observed masses include varying amounts of interaction energy.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: But despite such results, it is still conceivable that there could in the end be simple relations between truly fundamental particle masses—since it turns out that the masses that have actually been observed in effect also include varying amounts of interaction energy.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 9, “Fundamental Physics”; section “Elementary Particles” (from p. 525), p. 528. Scope: masses of elementary particles such as leptons and quarks

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch09-23: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.68

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: High-quality mass measurements exist and proposed relations are easy to check. They cannot by themselves separate intrinsic mass from interaction energy or prevent flexible post hoc numerology, so only model-specific versions are resolvable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Fit specified simple integer or algebraic mass relations to renormalized particle-mass estimates under a defined theory of interaction energy, with penalties for relation complexity and multiple testing. Stable predictive relations would support the claim; failure across justified decompositions would weaken it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Simple ratios can be found post hoc among many possibilities.

Quark masses depend on renormalization scheme and scale.

'Truly fundamental mass' is model-dependent.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.75
operationalizability: 0.55
data adequacy: 0.7
data existence: 0.95
discriminating power: 0.4

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Observed masses are public and precise, and it is immediate that they do not lie in simple ratios. The claim retreats to unknown fundamental masses after subtracting a scheme-dependent interaction energy, so the tables test only the surface reading. The hedged remainder is not fixed tightly enough for those tables to confirm or refute it.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Test published lepton and quark masses for simple rational or other pre-registered relations, then repeat the test on a stated definition of mass with interaction energy removed. Simple relations among observed masses would confirm the strong reading; their absence only touches the claim if the interaction-energy subtraction is fixed in advance.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
How much of a measured mass is interaction energy depends on the renormalization scheme.

'May' plus an allowance for interaction energy makes the claim hard to refute.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

data existence: 0.9
operationalizability: 0.4
analysis feasibility: 0.72
